title: tracker-audit --gate g1,g4 now reports 4 findings on HEAD, not the 3 the manifest's C10 evidence claims — the 4th is a new, undisclosed, self-referential G4 hit caused by this unit's own manifest quoting a prior tracker-audit paste verbatim
evidence: Checker re-ran `node scripts/tracker-audit.mjs --gate g1,g4` on HEAD (8e862f5): 4 findings — the same G1 (T-033 status drift) and the same two G4 rows (t-033-bot-tests.md, t-047-controller.md) the manifest names, PLUS a new G4 row: 'qa/manifests/t-031-audio-watchdog.md cites ISS-001, ISS-002 bare...'. Re-ran the identical command in a throwaway `git worktree add --detach` at base commit 986fcd8: exactly 3 findings, byte-identical to the manifest's pasted output (confirming the manifest's paste WAS accurate at the time it was taken, before its own file existed in the tree). qa/manifests/t-031-audio-watchdog.md does not itself discuss ISS-001/ISS-002 as its own issues — it merely quotes, in its 'Actual outputs' and 'Known pre-existing failures' sections, the SAME tracker-audit output the manifest is citing as pre-existing evidence for t-033-bot-tests.md/t-047-controller.md, and tracker-audit's G4 check pattern-matches that quoted text as if the manifest itself were making an ambiguous bare ISS-001/ISS-002 claim.
reproduction: cd D:/KnowledgeBase-lanes/t-031-audio-watchdog && node scripts/tracker-audit.mjs --gate g1,g4 (4 findings) vs. git worktree add --detach <scratch> 986fcd8 && node scripts/tracker-audit.mjs --gate g1,g4 (3 findings, byte-identical to manifest's paste)
fix_direction: Either tighten tracker-audit.mjs's G4 pattern to skip text inside a manifest's own quoted-evidence/code-block sections (so documenting a prior finding doesn't itself trigger a new one), or have manifests that must quote a prior tracker-audit paste do so inside a fenced block G4 explicitly excludes. Not a functional regression in the T-031 feature itself — purely a self-referential artifact of the audit tool's naive substring match colliding with the contract's own C10 exception-clause requirement to quote prior findings verbatim.
